chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ؛ وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعًا عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ، عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father; and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنْتُ قَاعِدًا إِلَى جَنْبِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَهُوَ مُحْتَبٍ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْكَعْبَةِ، فَقَالَ: أَمَا إِنَّ النَّظَرَ إِلَيْهَا عِبَادَةٌ، فَجَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَجِيلَةَ يُقَالُ لَهُ: عَاصِمُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، فَقَالَ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: إِنَّ كَعْبَ الْأَحْبَارِ كَانَ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْكَعْبَةَ تَسْجُدُ لِبَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ فِي كُلِّ غَدَاةٍ، فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: فَمَا تَقُولُ فِيمَا قَالَ كَعْبُ؟ فَقَالَ: صَدَقَ، الْقَوْلُ مَا قَالَ كَعْبُ، فَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: كَذَبْتَ وَكَذَبَ كَعْبُ الْأَحْبَارِ مَعَكَ وَغَضَبَ، قَالَ زُرَارَةُ: مَا رَأَيْتُهُ اسْتَقْبَلَ أَحَدًا بِقَوْلِ كَذَبْتَ غَيْرَهُ …

translations.en: I was seated at the side of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was seated with his legs drawn up to his belly, facing the Ka'ba. He said: 'Indeed, looking at it is a form of worship.' Then a man from Bajila, called 'Asim ibn Umar, came to him and said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Ka'b al-Ahbar used to say: The Ka'ba prostrates to Bayt al-Maqdis every morning.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your opinion about what Ka'b said?' He said: 'He spoke the truth – it is as Ka'b said.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You have lied, and Ka'b al-Ahbar has lied with you,' and he became angry. Zurara said: 'I had never seen him saying to someone

en.summary: This hadith highlights the spiritual merit of contemplating the Ka'ba while establishing a nuanced scholarly debate on the physical prostration of the Ka'ba to the Bayt al-Maqdis, a view attributed to Ka'b al-Ahbar. Imam al-Sadiq’s rare declaration of 'you have lied' underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between accepted traditions and the specific interpretations of the Jewish scholar, reflecting the broader context of inter-sectarian theological dialogue in early Islam.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on looking at the Ka'ba and what did Imam al-Sadiq say about Ka'b al-Ahbar's claim of its prostration?

key_terms.كَعْبُ الْأَحْبَارِ: Ka'b al-Ahbar (a Jewish scholar whose views were often cited)
